       1             SENATOR ZELDIN:  Good morning, everybody.

       2             Thank you for being here on this morning here

       3      in Albany to have a hearing on organized retail

       4      crime.

       5             The general rationale for an

       6      "organized retail crime" legislative package is --

       7      you know, this isn't just something that

       8      New York State is suffering from.

       9             Really, all across this country, over --

      10      almost $30 billion a year, annually, is being

      11      stolen, 15 billion of which is the approximation for

      12      supermarkets.  And, additionally, state and local

      13      governments are losing out on tens of millions of

      14      dollars annually in lost sales tax and excise-fee

      15      revenue.

      16             Organized retail crime is a public health and

      17      safety issue.  The item stolen are often resold to

      18      unsuspecting wholesalers who, in turn, sell the

      19      stolen items to consumers.

      20             Many of the heavily trafficked items require

      21      proper handling, such as storage at certain

      22      temperatures, which may not be occurring when the

      23      product is in the hands of thieves.

      24             Also, organized retail-crime thieves have

      25      been known to change the expiration date of products





 

                                                                   4
       1      by repackaging them, thereby posing further health

       2      and safety risks.

       3             There's a package of six bills that the

       4      Consumer Protection Committee passed last week, and

       5      finally put some teeth into the crackdown on

       6      organized retail crime.

       7             These six bills, which I believe that,

       8      Michael Rosen, our first speaker, is going to get

       9      into a little further depth on, these six particular

      10      bills are sponsored in the Assembly by

      11      Assemblyman Mike Cusick.

      12             Not only are we defining what "organized

      13      retail crime" is, but we're addressing some of the

      14      concerns of prosecutors who are dealing with the

      15      challenges; for example, of jurisdiction.

      16             Jurisdictional challenges:  When a particular

      17      a crime takes place in their county, it might be

      18      part of a larger pattern of misconduct.  They can

      19      only charge for that specific crime, and not so much

      20      the pattern.

      21             So, we tried to deal with that.

      22             We also have individuals that are aware of

      23      limits, say $1,000, in order to qualify as a grand

      24      larceny in the -- if someone, you know, is only

      25      stealing $900 from one particular location, and





 

                                                                   5
       1      stealing $900 from another location, they're coming

       2      under the $1,000 limit for grand larceny.

       3             But, if it's part of a pattern of organized

       4      retail theft, it really should be charged as if over

       5      $1,000 was stolen.

       6             These are very complex enterprises.

       7             Some of our individuals that are testifying

       8      today will get into a little bit more detail about

       9      it, but it really starts at the most local levels,

      10      with small teams that are going into a particular

      11      store.

      12             You might have an individual that's loading

      13      up a shopping cart.  Maybe someone else is outside,

      14      getting ready to drive away in the getaway car.

      15      Maybe someone was pulled off the street and given a

      16      couple hundred bucks to come in and be the one to

      17      push the shopping cart out the front.

      18             It really depends on how that team is set up.

      19             But what starts at this very small local

      20      level gets very complex, because these goods are

      21      getting passed up, they end up in warehouses.

      22      Warehouses are packed, wall to wall, with stolen

      23      products.

      24             These are products that we find on the

      25      Internet, sometimes in flea markets.

      15             I represent Price Chopper Supermarkets, and

       1      dollars nationwide, each year.

      24      whenever we have pictures available through our

      25      internal surveillance, as well as data or detail on

       1      license plate numbers or any other information that

       2      we can procure.  And then we provide that to the

       3      network, to help to identify these individuals, and

       4      help to -- help law enforcement prosecute those

       5      perpetrators.

       6             Over this past year, we have identified close

       7      to 60 percent of our external theft as being

       8      ORC-related.

       9             The amounts -- this amounts to about

      10      $2 million to our company alone over this past year.

      11             There was 659 cases that were identified as

      12      ORC.  And there are a lot of cases that we don't get

      13      enough information to be able to identify.  So,

      14      there's a lot of theft going on that we're not made

      15      aware of or we don't have information on.

      16             Since the time we have been tracking ORC

      17      cases, we have identified thefts that involve

      18      high-profile products, such as razor blades, baby

      19      formula, dental whitening strips, body wash, and,

      20      fresh product, like meat and seafood.

      22      Tide detergent, which has become a new form of what

      23      is referred to as "street currency."

      24             The product that is stolen is then resold for

      25      cash at bodegas, mom-and-pop stores, pawn shops,

       1      flea markets, and even online on eBay and

       2      Craigslist.

       3             We have also seen a rise in organized crime

       4      involving credit cards, gift cards, fraudulent

       5      couponing, price-ticket switching, and fraudulent

       6      product returns using fake receipts.

       7             As an example:  During this past month, we

       8      have been investigating an ORC group hitting our

       9      capital-district stores for baby formula.

      10             This group consists of two, three, or

      11      four individuals at a time, loading baby formula

      12      into reusable bags, and exiting the store without

      13      paying.

      14             Two subjects out of approximately seven known

      15      individuals are presently being prosecuted.

      16             The police have not been able to identify the

      17      others involved.

      18             The total case value of the linked incidents

      19      is over $5,700, which by dollar amount would be a

      20      felony.

      21             However, due to the jurisdictional issues,

      22      each incident is only prosecutable on its own as a

      23      misdemeanor.

      25      occurred in our stores in Brunswick and Troy, which

       2      Niscayuna, Schenectady County; and Saratoga,

       4             This type of case clearly demonstrates our

       5      frustration with the present laws.

       6             These individuals know how to work the

       7      system, and travel no more than 10 to 15 minutes

       8      from store to store, knowing that there are no

       1      stores using fake receipts.

      21             Good morning.

      22             My name is Justin Dietel, and I'm an

      23      asset-protection specialist at (SRS) ShopRite.

      24             We are a full-service grocery store operating

      25      in New York and New Jersey.





 

                                                                   16
       1             We operate a total of 31 stores, with 28 of

       2      them in New York, from Yonkers to Liberty, up to the

      11             Over the last several years, all retailers

      13             ShopRite has not been immune to this.

      15      razor blades, baby formula, Red Bull, meat, seafood,

      17             We have even experienced some losses on

       1      will request certain items.
